text:
jamie: Hey @priya — saw the support ticket (T-8421). To triage the auth + latency spike quickly, can you paste one failing request_id and run one of these minimal repros? Prefer curl or one-line SDK snippet so we capture client timing and response headers.

jamie: Minimal curl (captures headers + timing):
```
curl -i -D - 'https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"hi","max_tokens":5}' \
  --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 20 --write-out "\nTIME_TOTAL:%{time_total}\n" -o /tmp/resp_body.txt
```

jamie: This prints TIME_TOTAL and saves body; please paste the HTTP headers (the -i/-D output) and the TIME_TOTAL line. Also copy the value of `x-request-id` (or `x-redwood-request-id`) from the response headers.

jamie: If using Python (httpx) please run this minimal snippet and paste stdout:
```
import httpx, os, time
k=os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY")
start=time.time()
r=httpx.post("https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate", json={"model":"redwood-1","input":"hi","max_tokens":5}, headers={"Authorization":f"Bearer {k}"}, timeout=20.0)
print(r.status_code, r.headers.get("x-request-id"), r.elapsed.total_seconds())
print(r.headers)
print(r.text[:1000])
```

jamie: Node/Fetch:
```
const res = await fetch("https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate", {method:"POST", headers:{"Authorization":`Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}`,"Content-Type":"application/json"}, body:JSON.stringify({model:"redwood-1", input:"hi", max_tokens:5}),});
console.log(res.status, res.headers.get('x-request-id'));
console.log('time:', /* measure using process.hrtime or client lib */);
console.log(await res.text());
```

jamie: Go (net/http):
```
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 20*time.Second)
req, _ := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, "POST", "https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate", bytes.NewBuffer(payload))
req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+os.Getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
client := &http.Client{}
start := time.Now()
resp, err := client.Do(req)
fmt.Println("err", err, "status", resp.StatusCode, "x-request-id", resp.Header.Get("x-request-id"), "t", time.Since(start))
```

jamie: Extra asks: SDK version, region (if you pinned one), app server time vs client time, and paste the request_id you see in headers. If you have server logs, include the local timestamp for the request_id. Thanks :pray:

priya: thanks — ran the curl above. output:
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
x-request-id: rs-20250401-7f9c
content-type: application/json

TIME_TOTAL:2.73
body: {"error":"token_expired","message":"token expired"}

priya: SDK is python-requests on a lambda (eu-west-1), token issued ~2025-04-01T08:15:03Z, request timestamp 2025-04-01T08:15:12Z. attaching the tiny curl output.

mike: @jamie can you check backend logs for rs-20250401-7f9c? looks like token expiry but 2.7s latency — might be issuing fallback call to auth provider.

ashley: if token refresh is happening we might see a cascade. @priya please also run the curl with the header `X-Debug-Trace: 1` — this will add server timing headers for us (no PII). e.g.: `-H "X-Debug-Trace: 1"` and paste the extra timing headers.

priya: OK will run and paste back in 5.

support-bot: [automated] Created incident-9812 and forwarded rs-20250401-7f9c to eng-oncall.

jamie: thanks — once you paste the X-Debug-Trace response we'll check if the high time is at auth exchange vs model route. If it's only auth we can suggest longer token TTL or local caching as workaround.

priya: pasted new output: headers include `x-auth-latency: 2.5`, `x-routing-latency: 0.1`, `x-request-id: rs-20250401-7f9c`. body unchanged (401).
